evidence_type: direct assay (cDNA isolation and genomic sequencing)
claim_tested: Is the Q16609 132 aa ORF an intact coding frame?
key_finding: Loss of a canonical splice donor at a skipped exon causes a coding frameshift and premature stop codons; the isolated liver transcript encodes only a signal peptide plus one kringle
context: Human liver cDNA and genomic DNA
confidence_and_limitations: High. Single laboratory; no protein was detected; the 132 aa product is a conceptual translation

claim_tested: Is LPAL2 a transcribed member of the apo(a)/plasminogen cluster?
key_finding: The cluster contains apo(a) and plasminogen plus two apo(a)-related genes or pseudogenes; apo(a)rg-C is transcribed in human liver
context: Human genomic YAC clones and liver RNA
confidence_and_limitations: High for transcription and locus structure; the authors already label these loci as genes or pseudogenes

claim_tested: Where does the apo(a) lineage that produced LPAL2 come from?
key_finding: The human apo(a) type evolved from a duplicated plasminogen gene during recent primate evolution; apo(a) is confined to a subset of primates
confidence_and_limitations: High for the LPA lineage; the paper does not analyse LPAL2 directly

claim_tested: Does Q16609 protein bind other proteins in vivo?
key_finding: One binary interaction with VAC14 (Q08AM6) from a proteome-scale Y2H map; basis of a GO:0005515 IPI annotation
context: Yeast two-hybrid with human ORFeome constructs
confidence_and_limitations: Low for endogenous relevance. Tests a forced ORF construct in yeast and cannot show that the polypeptide exists in human cells

claim_tested: Does Q16609 protein bind other proteins in vivo?
key_finding: Five further binary interactions (HIP1 CLSTN1-2 CCK CASP6 RAN) feeding five GO:0005515 IPI annotations
confidence_and_limitations: Low for endogenous relevance. Partner set is incoherent for a secreted kringle protein and suggests non-specific binding

key_finding: Protein existence level 5 Uncertain; CAUTION comment states it could be the product of a pseudogene; the entry carries only a predicted signal peptide and kringle
confidence_and_limitations: High as a curated statement; it is a database judgement not an experiment

key_finding: HGNC locus_type pseudogene; the only RefSeq transcript carries an NR_ non-coding prefix; NCBI Gene 80350 states all transcripts have a truncated ORF and are NMD candidates
confidence_and_limitations: High. Independent of UniProt and consistent across HGNC NCBI and Ensembl

claim_tested: Does the annotated locus produce a translatable transcript?
key_finding: Biotype transcribed_unprocessed_pseudogene with no Translation; recomputed translation gives 222 codons then TAG followed by 26 more in-frame stops over the remaining 73% of the transcript
confidence_and_limitations: High for the computation; depends on the accuracy of the single annotated transcript model

claim_tested: Is the ORF intact in other primates?
key_finding: Chimpanzee bonobo gorilla and the reconstructed Hsap-Ppan-Ptro and Ggor-Hsap-Ppan-Ptro ancestors all carry the identical premature TAG at codon 223 with identical flanks; only one small bonobo indel elsewhere
confidence_and_limitations: High for African apes; orangutan aligns only over exons 1 to 3 so its status at the stop is unknown. Tandem kringle repeats carry some paralogy risk

claim_tested: Is the reading frame under purifying selection?
key_finding: Nonsynonymous substitutions match the local intronic neutral rate (obs/exp 1.03 chimpanzee 0.91 bonobo 1.13 gorilla); synonymous substitutions are 3.5 to 3.9 fold above neutral so raw dN/dS of 0.25 to 0.29 is an artefact
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. Only 7 to 12 nonsynonymous differences per pair so the test has limited power to exclude weak constraint

claim_tested: Is LPAL2 loss-of-function intolerant in humans?
key_finding: No constraint record exists for LPAL2 because it is modelled as a pseudogene; LPA oe_lof 1.005 pLI 2e-68 and PLG oe_lof 0.393 pLI 0.76 for comparison
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. The absence of a metric is a consequence of the pseudogene call and so is not independent evidence

claim_tested: Could mass spectrometry ever distinguish an LPAL2 protein from apo(a) or plasminogen?
key_finding: 13 of 17 Q16609 tryptic peptides are not verbatim substrings of apo(a) or plasminogen so discriminating peptides exist; UniProt lists no PeptideAtlas cross-reference for the entry
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Peptide uniqueness was assessed by exact substring matching only; PeptideAtlas was not queried directly

claim_tested: Does any primate lineage keep an open LPAL2 reading frame?
key_finding: No lineage reads past codon 242. African apes share TAG at codon 223; Macaca nemestrina has Glu there but stops at 242; Papio Cercocebus Mandrillus and both Rhinopithecus have the position deleted; New World monkeys tarsier and strepsirrhines stop at codons 184 to 214. Frameshifting deletions of 25 bp (macaque) to 96 bp (Otolemur) in every non-ape lineage
context: 19 primate genomes with reconstructed ancestral nodes
confidence_and_limitations: High for the alignment itself. The non-ape rows may be the pre-duplication ancestral locus rather than LPAL2 orthologues, since apo(a) is confined to a subset of primates. Orangutan exons 4 and 5 are absent even from EPO_EXTENDED

claim_tested: Is the cross-species similarity a gene conversion tract from LPA?
key_finding: Human LPAL2 kringle is 97.5% identical to chimpanzee and 97.5% to gorilla LPAL2, but only 89.0% to the closest human paralogue LPA kringle IV-8 and 87.8% to the bulk of the KIV array. Orthologues exceed the best paralogue by 8.5 points, opposite to the concerted evolution prediction
context: 237 nt kringle region, EPO alignment and Ensembl genomic sequence
confidence_and_limitations: High. Rejects recent interlocus gene conversion. Does not exclude conversion predating the human-gorilla split, though such an event would also predate the shared stop codon

claim_tested: Is the LPAL2 locus transcribed, and in which tissues?
key_finding: LPAL2 (ENSG00000213071.11) liver median 7.95 TPM, the top tissue, 25.2-fold above the 0.315 TPM median of the other 53 tissues; next are Testis 1.86 and Artery_Aorta 1.63. Same liver-dominant pattern as LPA (liver 14.98) and PLG (liver 323.04). GTEx geneType is transcribed unprocessed pseudogene
confidence_and_limitations: High for transcription, and it corroborates the liver cDNA of PMID:7749817 and PMID:8148351. Transcription is orthogonal to translation and does not support coding status

claim_tested: Is there peptide-level evidence for a Q16609 product?
key_finding: No result obtainable. PeptideAtlas GetProteins returns an anti-botnet interstitial page; the EBI Proteins API /proteomics endpoint returns empty records for Q16609 and for the positive controls P08519 and P00747; the Human Protein Atlas search API returns an empty list for LPAL2; EBI Expression Atlas returns HTTP 404
context: Public API access from this session
confidence_and_limitations: None. Recorded as inaccessible resources, not as absence of peptide evidence, because the same endpoints are empty for abundant plasma plasminogen

claim_tested: Is the LPAL2 reading frame intact in orangutan, the one great ape no multiple alignment covers?
key_finding: Pongo abelii carries an independent premature TAG at codon 166 where human reads TGG (Trp). The substitution sits in exon 4, which aligns one-to-one over all 158 nt with zero indels. The human codon-223 position is deleted in orangutan, and the orangutan 731 nt frame has 2 in-frame stops against 1 in human. All five great apes therefore have a disabled frame, by two separate mutations
context: Ensembl Compara pairwise LASTZ_NET, Pongo abelii genome
confidence_and_limitations: High. A single substitution call inside an indel-free exon does not depend on gap placement. Depends on the orangutan assembly being correct at this repeat-rich locus

claim_tested: Can the Nei-Gojobori plus local-neutral-rate test detect purifying selection when it is present?
key_finding: PLG nonsynonymous observed/expected 0.353 (95% CI 0.14 to 0.73, p=0.00087) against chimpanzee and 0.521 (0.24 to 0.99, p=0.023) against gorilla, using the same EPO alignment and its own intronic calibration (1.37% and 1.38%). The same test gives 1.026, 0.909 and 1.127 at LPAL2. LPAL2 lower 95% bounds 0.44, 0.37 and 0.57 sit at or above the PLG point estimates
context: Human versus chimpanzee and gorilla, PLG canonical CDS ENST00000872438
confidence_and_limitations: High as a methodological control. 14 of 21 PLG CDS exons were recoverable from EPO, so the control covers a subset of the gene. Weak constraint at LPAL2 is still not excluded

claim_tested: Is there mass-spectrometry evidence for a Q16609 polypeptide?
key_finding: Zero MS1 records for Q16609 across tissues and fluids. In the identical query, P08519 apo(a) returns 44 tissues, P00747 plasminogen 70 (liver normalised intensity 5.01), P02768 albumin 79 and P68871 haemoglobin beta 71. The apo(a) control is the low-abundance close paralogue whose kringle sequence Q16609 shares
context: Human tissues and body fluids, shotgun mass spectrometry
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. A genuine negative with working internal controls, unlike the blocked or empty resources. Shotgun coverage depends on the search database, and the 13 Q16609-discriminating tryptic peptides may never have been searched for
